stories.title: Christian Cage and AEW vs WWE Rivalry
stories.tldr: Chris Jericho stated that AEW has always followed its own path and never copied WWE, pointing to their matches, ratings, and ticket sales as proof. However, Eric Bischoff strongly disagreed with Jericho's comments, calling them "bullshit" and arguing that AEW has spent years since 2019 creating an "us versus them" narrative against WWE. Jericho explained his decision to stay with AEW rather than sign with WWE, citing his personal investment in helping start the company and his working relationship with Tony Khan.

stories.title: Tweets and Social Media Moments
stories.tldr: Professional wrestling's social media landscape delivered another week of entertaining moments, from Liv Morgan's playful escape from Iyo Sky to Rey Fenix celebrating a championship with Wile E. Coyote. The highlights also included Chelsea Green enjoying Disney World despite a broken face, wrestlers engaging in backstage antics, and heartwarming charitable acts. These moments showcase the humor and personality wrestlers bring to their fan interactions beyond the ring.

stories.title: Kyle Fletcher and Mark Davis Individual Success
stories.tldr: Kyle Fletcher and Mark Davis have transitioned from their six-year run as the tag team Aussie Open into successful individual careers in AEW without turning on each other. Both wrestlers remain part of The Don Callis Family faction while pursuing singles success, which Fletcher considers a unique and positive development in professional wrestling.

stories.title: Dustin Rhodes Social Media Interaction
stories.tldr: Dustin Rhodes sharply rejected being tagged in a pizza debate about pickles as a topping, telling the fan to stop "hate tweeting" him. The AEW veteran has a documented history of strongly opposing unconventional pizza toppings, particularly pineapple, and apparently pickles have now joined his list of pizza no-nos.

stories.title: Christian Cage AEW Collision Line
stories.tldr: Christian Cage delivered the line of the night on AEW Collision by responding to Matt Jackson's comment that Cope and Christian are old enough to be his father with a deadpan "Who says I'm not?" Meanwhile, Will Ospreay secured partners from New Japan Pro Wrestling's United Empire to face the Callis Family in a trios match on Dynamite, setting up a busy card for August 19.

stories.title: Rumor Look Back February 2026
stories.tldr: A wrestling news roundup from February 2026 examined rumors from six months prior, tracking their accuracy regarding WrestleMania 42 preparations, AEW's Double or Nothing venue announcement, and various wrestler contract negotiations and injury updates. Seth Rollins' return and Bron Breakker's comeback were confirmed, while Bad Bunny to WWE and other predictions proved inaccurate. The report showed mixed results with some insider reports proving accurate while others missed the mark entirely.

stories.title: Bandido Arena Mexico Performance
stories.tldr: Bandido revealed new details about a four-year ban from Arena Mexico due to his AAA affiliation, which was recently lifted through AEW's partnership with CMLL. The ROH World Champion also compared the venue's significance to other legendary wrestling destinations like Madison Square Garden and the Tokyo Dome.

stories.title: Nigel McGuinness Injury on AEW Collision
stories.tldr: Nigel McGuinness' injury status remains uncertain as AEW prepares to reveal more details during Monday's Continental Challenge Cup selection show on YouTube. The quarterfinal bracket is taking shape with eight competitors already confirmed, though McGuinness could be forced out depending on the severity of his injury.

stories.title: Swerve Strickland AEW All In Opponent
stories.tldr: Rather than pursuing a trios championship opportunity, Swerve Strickland appears headed for a singles match against Jungle Boy at AEW All In after the two had a backstage confrontation on Collision. Jungle Boy, emboldened by his competitive loss to Jon Moxley, challenged Strickland as part of a new character direction to face former world champions and prove he belongs at the top level.

stories.title: JBL WWE Anecdotes and Commentary
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer JBL recently shared multiple anecdotes on his podcast, including how attending a Super Bowl in Arizona cost him $7,500 in fines when weather canceled flights and forced expensive alternative travel. He also discussed why a two-night Royal Rumble format makes business sense and reflected on Brock Lesnar's legendary career following his recent WWE retirement.

stories.title: Slick Open-Heart Surgery Recovery
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Slick, the legendary "Doctor of Style" manager whose real name is Kenneth Johnson, suffered a heart attack and underwent emergency open-heart surgery on August 16, 2026, ironically on the anniversary of his WWF debut. The 40-year wrestling veteran is currently recovering in the ICU, and while his recovery is progressing slowly, he successfully made it to the hospital in time and survived the surgery.

stories.title: Drake Wuertz Apology for Controversial Past
stories.tldr: Former WWE NXT referee Drake Wuertz made a public apology at GCW Homecoming for his controversial past, including anti-mask activism, QAnon-adjacent social media activity, and associations with conspiracy-related groups. Wuertz acknowledged that fans had valid reasons to be upset with him and asked for an opportunity to prove he has changed, crediting friends like Joey Janela and Brett Lauderdale for trying to reach him years ago. WWE released Wuertz in May 2021 amid the controversies, though the company never officially stated his departure was due to his political views and outside activities.

stories.title: Eric Bischoff on Roman Reigns and WWE
stories.tldr: Eric Bischoff has praised Roman Reigns' natural star power and aura, claiming nobody in WWE or AEW possesses his level of charisma and presence, despite earlier criticism of his creative direction. Bischoff also asserted that top stars like Reigns and Brock Lesnar have significant creative control over their characters in WWE, comparing the situation to Hulk Hogan's influence in WCW.

stories.title: WWE Raw Lineup Announcements
stories.tldr: WWE Raw General Manager Adam Pearce announced an updated lineup for Monday's show in Buffalo, New York on August 17, 2026, featuring Intercontinental Champion Chad Gable defending his title against Hall of Famer Rey Mysterio. The card also includes Sol Ruca facing Lyra Valkyria, two World Heavyweight Championship tournament first-round matches, and appearances by Roman Reigns and Jey Uso, with approximately 9,020 tickets distributed for the event at KeyBank Center.

stories.title: Maven WWE Career Retrospective
stories.tldr: Former WWE talent Maven Huffman recently discussed professional wrestling safety on his YouTube channel, specifically addressing the proper technique for chair shots during matches. He explained that aiming for the meaty portion of a wrestler's back is ideal because it creates visual impact while minimizing long-term injury risk compared to striking the head. Maven drew from his own experience, recalling taking a chair shot from The Undertaker following his 2002 Royal Rumble elimination of the legendary wrestler.

stories.title: Kylie Rae WWE ID Return
stories.tldr: Kylie Rae returned to professional wrestling on August 16, 2026, competing for Girl Fight against Ashlyn Alexander, marking her first match in over a year. She had vacated the WWE ID Women's Championship in September 2025 after announcing her pregnancy, and WWE subsequently declined to renew her contract while she was pregnant, a decision that drew significant criticism for its poor optics.

stories.title: Brock Lesnar WWE Theme Fan Remix
stories.tldr: A fan-created remix has added lyrics to Brock Lesnar's iconic WWE entrance theme, and the creative take has resonated strongly with wrestling fans. The 51-second video has accumulated nearly 200,000 views on Twitter, demonstrating how well the added vocals mesh with the instrumental classic. While WWE is unlikely to alter such a recognizable theme in reality, the edit offers an interesting glimpse into what an alternative version might sound like.

stories.title: WWE Free Agents Report
stories.tldr: WWE currently has six official free agents on its roster who can appear across all brands without being tied to a specific show. The article proposes five additional wrestlers who could benefit from free agent status, including Drew McIntyre, Carmelo Hayes, Fraxiom, Keanu Carver, and Bayley, each for different strategic reasons related to their current booking situations and character development.

stories.title: Lola Vice NXT to Main Roster Call-Up Hints
stories.tldr: Lola Vice posted a cryptic "loading…" message on Twitter on August 16, 2026, which fans interpret as another hint about her imminent WWE main roster call-up. WWE creative has already begun discussing plans for her move, with SmackDown being the rumored destination, following several other signs that her NXT tenure is ending.

stories.title: Zaria on NXT Women's Work Ethic
stories.tldr: NXT Women's North American Champion Zaria claims the women's division at the WWE Performance Center works harder than the men, both physically and emotionally. She credits this work ethic and willingness to tap into emotions as reasons why NXT's women's division has become the best in professional wrestling, with Bully Ray corroborating her observations from his time filming WWE LFG.

stories.title: Nikki Cross Money in the Bank and Title Win
stories.tldr: Nikki Cross reflected on her accomplishments as "Nikki A.S.H." including winning the Money in the Bank briefcase and cashing it in for the WWE Raw Women's Championship. Cross expressed gratitude for the opportunity to be the top woman in the company and revealed she found out late about both wins. She recalled the nerves and excitement of cashing in during a RAW episode and celebrated the importance of fan support in professional wrestling.

stories.title: WWE World Heavyweight Championship Succession
stories.tldr: Roman Reigns has held the WWE World Heavyweight Championship since WrestleMania 42, defeating CM Punk in the main event. With Reigns positioned far ahead of the roster, only a select few wrestlers have realistic chances of dethroning him. The article ranks five potential challengers, with Oba Femi considered the favorite to eventually become the next World Heavyweight Champion, possibly at WrestleMania 43.

stories.title: Chelsea Green and Unreal Similarities Discovery
stories.tldr: Chelsea Green won the Interim WWE Women's Championship at SummerSlam and has since discovered striking similarities to former WWE Champions Daniel Bryan and Kofi Kingston. The comparisons, pointed out by Triple H and fans after the release of UNREAL Season 1, relate not to wrestling ability but to how intensely their fanbases have rallied behind them. Green credits her character work and fan support for her championship success, noting she has received congratulations from wrestling legends like Mick Foley and X-Pac.

stories.title: Becky Lynch and Finn Balor Favorite Matches
stories.tldr: Becky Lynch and Finn Balor discussed their favorite matches during an interview in Dublin, with Lynch choosing her WrestleMania 38 clash against Bianca Belair and Balor selecting a non-televised NXT Championship bout against Samoa Joe from 2016. Both wrestlers revealed they don't watch their own matches back, instead relying on instinct and memory to judge their performances.

stories.title: Trick Williams Theme Song Significance
stories.tldr: Trick Williams has emphasized that his "Whoop That Trick" chant is far more significant than just a theme song, representing a lifetime of personal and professional evolution. The organic fan chant originated during his NXT days and has continued on the main roster, connecting his birth name Matrick—a combination of his parents' names—with his wrestling identity and the cultural reference from the 2005 film "Hustle & Flow."

stories.title: CM Punk and Finn Balor WWE Collaboration
stories.tldr: Finn Balor has praised CM Punk as a "super professional" and easy-to-work-with performer following their two matches in early 2026, contradicting Punk's reputation for past conflicts with peers. Despite his history of contentious relationships in wrestling, Punk appears to be a changed person in his WWE return, according to multiple wrestlers and company officials. Balor expressed eagerness to face Punk again in the future.

stories.title: Jacob Fatu WWE Debut and Michael Hayes Advice
stories.tldr: Jacob Fatu revealed on a podcast with Stephanie McMahon that WWE Hall of Famer Michael Hayes gave him crucial pre-debut advice about leaving his past accomplishments behind and not overestimating his popularity. The story includes an amusing anecdote about Hayes insisting Fatu wear a ski mask during his debut, which Triple H quickly overruled during a live show, leading to Fatu removing the mask on his instruction.

stories.title: Bully Ray ECW Hall of Fame Nomination
stories.tldr: Bully Ray recently called for his former ECW stablemate Spike Dudley to be inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame, crediting Spike with helping elevate the careers of numerous wrestlers through his willingness to take significant bumps and serve as a reliable opponent. Bully highlighted several iconic moments involving Spike, including his involvement in major debuts and angles with legends like Bam Bam Bigelow, Brock Lesnar, and The Undertaker, and praised Spike's role in the success of the Dudley Boyz tag team.

stories.title: Blake Monroe WWE Main Roster Plans
stories.tldr: Blake Monroe, who made her WWE main roster debut in May, has ambitious plans to retire several legendary women's wrestlers including the Bella Twins, Paige, and Trish Stratus. Despite respecting the veteran generation, Monroe expressed her intentions to benefit from their careers while acknowledging their kindness and professionalism backstage. Monroe also revealed that much of what viewers see on "Total Divas" is authentic rather than scripted, and praised veterans like Brie Bella and Paige for their approachability.

stories.title: Chelsea Green WWE Women's Title Celebration
stories.tldr: Chelsea Green celebrated her interim Women's Championship by bringing it to Disney World over the weekend, posting photos with husband Matt Cardona. Meanwhile, Mickie James, the wife of GM Nick Aldis, praised Green's emotional promo during the medical clearance segment as one of the greatest promos she has ever witnessed.

stories.title: Zilla Fatu WWE Debut and Bloodline Role
stories.tldr: Bully Ray envisions Zilla Fatu as a potentially dominant "rogue" Bloodline member who could eventually challenge for Roman Reigns' spot atop WWE. Ray believes Fatu should take control of NXT the way Reigns dominates the main roster, while prior to his WWE signing, Fatu faced multiple AEW-affiliated stars including MJF, Brody King, and Mike Bailey across indie promotions.

stories.title: Marie Malenko Ring Name Change
stories.tldr: Marie Malenko has now been assigned the ring name "Kenzie" for her WWE NXT run. She continues working dark matches and live events, with her most recent bout coming against Kali Armstrong at an NXT house show in Melbourne, Florida in August.

stories.title: CM Punk NXT House Show Appearance
stories.tldr: CM Punk posted an emotional message on Instagram thanking Petersburg fans and the NXT roster following his appearance, expressing how much the experience meant to him. The house show saw a significant ticket sales boost, jumping from 1,261 distributed tickets before Punk's announcement to 2,135 by the day of the event.

stories.title: Chad Gable El Grande Americano Character Creation
stories.tldr: Chad Gable has revealed that the El Grande Americano gimmick was entirely his creative idea, designed to elevate an existing storyline with luchadors. A rotator cuff injury forced him away, allowing another wrestler to take over the character, creating an unexpected built-in narrative when Gable returned. Gable is now scheduled to defend his Intercontinental Championship against Rey Mysterio on August 17 WWE Raw.

stories.title: Shinsuke Nakamura Brings Mystery Partner
stories.tldr: A shadowy figure appeared in the background of Nakamura's latest promo, with fans identifying the silhouette as Hiromu Takahashi. The former IWGP Junior Heavyweight Champion departed NJPW in February and has been rumored for a WWE signing under the potential ring name Nox Raijin. Nakamura's cryptic warning to the MFTs suggests an imminent tag team challenge.

stories.title: Tiffany Stratton Swatting Incident and Interview
stories.tldr: During her livestream with N3on, Tiffany Stratton revealed her real name is Jessica Woynilko and explained that "Tiffany" comes from her mother's name. She addressed misconceptions that she doesn't care about wrestling, attributing them to her unconventional path into the industry, and reiterated her plan to wrestle for at least another decade until age 35.

stories.title: Rey Mysterio In-Ring Retirement Thoughts
stories.tldr: Rey Mysterio acknowledges his body is telling him it may be time to retire, but he's conflicted because he still enjoys wrestling more than his AAA GM duties. He's open to the possibility that retirement could happen suddenly, and he's accepting that younger talent will get opportunities ahead of him in the Lucha Libre world.

stories.title: Cody Rhodes Neck Tattoo Regret
stories.tldr: In a recent podcast appearance, Cody Rhodes opened up about his large neck tattoo, calling it "the greatest regret of my life" while acknowledging it has had some beneficial elements. Despite considering cover-up options, Rhodes has decided to keep the tattoo, saying he won't try to remove it and will "rock this until the end."

stories.title: Chad Gable IC Title Defense
stories.tldr: Chad Gable will defend his Intercontinental Championship against WWE Hall of Famer Rey Mysterio on Monday's Raw in Buffalo. The match marks Gable's first televised title defense since winning the IC Championship at SummerSlam. The show will also feature tournament matches for a World Heavyweight Championship challenger to face Roman Reigns in Mexico City.

stories.title: Paige WWE SmackDown Segment Cut
stories.tldr: WWE cut Paige's SmackDown segment for "logistical reasons" rather than creative decisions. The company later released the promo as a digital exclusive. Paige continued her war of words with Nikki Bella on social media, setting up a physical confrontation for the following week.

stories.title: Cody Rhodes vs Randy Orton WWE Main Event
stories.tldr: Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton will collide at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event on September 6 in Atlanta. The match was announced after Rhodes demanded the bout on SmackDown, leading to a chaotic brawl between the two rivals when Orton attacked Rhodes before his scheduled match with Sami Zayn.

stories.title: R-Truth WWE SmackDown Tag Title Match
stories.tldr: R-Truth and Damian Priest lost the WWE Tag Team Championship in a Triple Threat Match on SmackDown to MFT, who hit R-Truth with a double Powerbomb for the pinfall. The loss ended their 147-day championship reign. R-Truth apologized to both the WWE Universe and Priest on social media following the defeat.

stories.title: Jinder Mahal Indian Representation in WWE
stories.tldr: Mahal doubled down on his previous comments by highlighting specific emerging Indian talent, including Kevin Malik from his promotion WXM, whom he compared to Jeff Hardy for his enigmatic presence and athleticism. He emphasized that while Indian wrestling has potential, the country needs proper infrastructure and platforms to develop wrestlers capable of competing at WWE's elite level.

stories.title: El Grande Americano WWE Championship Match
stories.tldr: Rey Mysterio intervened in a backstage brawl between Dominik and El Grande Americano following the title match announcement. Chad Gable, the Original El Grande Americano, won the Intercontinental Championship at SummerSlam, creating a parallel storyline. Additionally, a #1 contender's tournament for Roman Reigns' World Heavyweight Championship has been announced for Raw in Mexico City on September 14, with semifinals and first-round matches now scheduled.

stories.title: Blake Monroe WWE SmackDown Debut Match
stories.tldr: Blake Monroe's match against Giulia still lacks an official date despite being made official by Nick Aldis. Monroe had initially requested a title shot against Chelsea Green for the WWE Women's Championship, but Giulia volunteered to face her instead, with Aldis approving the bout.

stories.title: Kevin Nash Reflecting on Wrestling Legends
stories.tldr: Kevin Nash is reflecting on his mortality and that of his wrestling peers as the only surviving member of the original NWO trio. With Scott Hall's 2022 death and Hulk Hogan's 2025 passing, Nash is grappling with the loss of his closest friends and the harsh reality that most of the wrestlers from his era are now gone. He's also recently quit drinking two years ago after deciding to be honest with himself about his health and lifestyle choices.

stories.title: NJPW G1 Climax 36 Awards and Results
stories.tldr: Ryohei Oiwa won the G1 Climax 36 tournament on August 16, defeating Yuya Uemura in the final via submission with his Big Lock headlock. Oiwa also took home the Technique Award, while Oleg Boltin won Outstanding Achievement and Yuto-Ice won Fighting Spirit. With the victory, Oiwa has earned a shot at IWGP Heavyweight Champion Yota Tsuji at King of Pro Wrestling in October.

stories.title: Julia Hart Stardom 5 Star Grand Prix
stories.tldr: Julia Hart's run in Stardom's 5 Star Grand Prix has concluded after she finished with eight points in the Blue Stars A Block, falling short of advancing to the knockout stage. Despite not winning the tournament, Hart reflected positively on her experience, stating she gained significant confidence throughout her time in the promotion. Hart won the Artist of Stardom Championship during the tour while also establishing herself as part of the Triangle of Madness stable with Thekla and Skye Blue.

stories.title: Bryan Danielson PNW Title Win and Show Reviews
stories.tldr: Bryan Danielson won the Relentless Pacific Northwest Championship this past weekend, marking a significant achievement that resonated with veteran wrestlers. The Bryan & Vinny Show podcast covered this title win along with reviews of recent WWE SmackDown and AEW Collision episodes, both of which featured noteworthy matches including Continental Challenge Cup competition.

stories.title: Shingo Takagi Calls Out Claudio Castagnoli
stories.tldr: Shingo Takagi blamed Claudio Castagnoli for throwing off his momentum heading into the G1 Climax 36 tournament, referencing a loss to PAC and Castagnoli on AEW Collision on July 2nd. With Takagi finishing the G1 with a 4-5 record, he called out Castagnoli to come to Kobe, Japan, for a match during NJPW's Destruction in Kobe event on September 27th, suggesting Castagnoli accompany his Death Riders stablemate Gabe Kidd who faces Drilla Moloney there.

stories.title: Drake Younger GCW Return and Apology
stories.tldr: Drake Younger returned to GCW and publicly apologized for his past controversial statements regarding COVID-19, masking, and his associations with groups he now acknowledges were inappropriate. Younger, a former NXT senior referee, was released from WWE in 2021 after attending events without a mask, criticizing vaccinations, and making controversial claims about mask mandates endangering children. During his GCW return, he took responsibility for his actions and said he hopes the audience will forgive him.

stories.title: Chris Jericho and CM Punk 2026 Storylines
stories.tldr: The latest Wrestling Observer Live Sunday episode covered Chris Jericho's current standing in AEW following a recent interview, CM Punk's newly announced celebration tour and the trend of similar promotional tours, updates on AEW Collision programming leading to All In, the whereabouts of the Motor City Machine Guns, and coverage of major news from the Women of Wrestling promotion.

stories.title: Dark Side of the Ring The Renegade
stories.tldr: A wrestling fan defends The Renegade, a WCW wrestler who was pushed as an Ultimate Warrior clone in 1995 despite being green in the ring. The article argues that WCW management knew the gimmick wouldn't work but proceeded anyway, then blamed Wilson afterward, rather than investing in his development at the Power Plant before a title push.

stories.title: Mark Henry Documentary
stories.tldr: A comprehensive documentary titled "World's Strongest Man | The Mark Henry Story" chronicles the legendary wrestler's journey from his humble beginnings in Silsby, Texas throughout his remarkable professional career. The film documents Henry's rise to becoming one of wrestling's most iconic and physically imposing figures. This documentary provides an in-depth look at both his personal life and his accomplishments in the professional wrestling industry.

stories.title: TNA Matt Hardy Comments on WWE Feud
stories.tldr: TNA's Matt Hardy has weighed in on the simmering WWE feud between Bron Breakker and Oba Femi, which has been building since SummerSlam. Hardy hopes the two powerhouses drag out their rivalry with compelling back-and-forth storytelling rather than rushing to a match. He also believes Femi should remain a babyface due to his popularity and the importance of having a prominent Black character represent the company in that capacity.

stories.title: The Rock Inducted as Disney Legend at D23
stories.tldr: Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson was inducted into Disney's 2026 Legend class at D23 in Anaheim, with Emily Blunt presenting the honor. Johnson delivered a heartfelt speech touching on his journey from humble beginnings, his role as a father, and his belief that kindness and treating people well matter more than fame itself. The induction adds to his already impressive resume as a WWE Champion, Hollywood star, producer, and voice of Maui in Disney's Moana franchise.

stories.title: Wrestling Fans And Wrestlers Rally Together To Raise Huge Amount For 18-Month-Old Boy Fighting Cancer
stories.tldr: The wrestling community came together for "Headlocks for Henry," a fundraiser event that raised over $10,000 approaching $11,000 for an 18-month-old boy battling Grade 3 Type A metastatic ependymoma. Organized by wrestler Matthew Robinson and supported by local businesses, wrestlers, and fans, the event at Jackson Live & Event Center in Seymour, Indiana demonstrated the power of community compassion in the face of childhood cancer.

stories.title: Mystery Wrestling 27 in Montreal, QC, Canada by Amber Nico Photo
stories.tldr: Mystery Wrestling 27 took place in Montreal, Quebec, Canada during the same weekend as AEW's Redemption event. The card featured several notable matches including Orange Cassidy versus Beef Wellington, a falls count anywhere match between Joey Janela and Cecil Nyx, and Johnny Mystery capturing the Mystery Wrestling championship.

stories.title: Malakai Black's Post-WWE Future
stories.tldr: Malakai Black remains a free agent with no confirmed destination as talks with MLW never progressed beyond preliminary contact. AEW has not indicated interest in his return. Black's only confirmed bookings are three PROGRESS Wrestling dates in September using the Malakai Black name.

stories.title: ALS Ice Bucket Challenge Fundraiser
stories.tldr: The wrestling community continues rallying behind Rebel with more Ice Bucket Challenge participants, including TNA's John Skyler and Cody Rhodes. Additional wrestlers and personalities like Adam Cole, Sting, and Tony Khan have joined the effort. AEW will host a special fundraiser episode called Rebel Heart on September 9 in Athens, Georgia.

stories.title: Joseph Sawyer GCW World Championship Win
stories.tldr: Joseph Sawyer is the 30th GCW World Champion, ending Atticus Cogar's 266-day reign that included 25 successful title defenses. Since his WWE release in April alongside Dexter Lumis, Nikki Cross, Erick Rowan and Bo Dallas, Sawyer has remained active on the independent circuit including a Canadian Championship challenge the night before his GCW title win.

stories.title: Jeff Cobb NJPW Return
stories.tldr: Jeff Cobb made his surprise NJPW return at the G1 Climax 36 finals on August 16, attacking former United Empire stablemate Callum Newman and officially joining Gedo's Unbound Company faction instead of rejoining his former group.

stories.title: TNA Interest in Josh Bishop
stories.tldr: TNA's interest in Josh Bishop has been confirmed as significant, with management specifically impressed by his Fourth Rope Wrestling performances. Bishop has prior TNA experience as a freelancer, including a Slammiversary 2025 pre-show victory in a 6-man tag team match alongside Real1 and Zilla Fatu.

stories.title: Alex Wright WCW Career Story
stories.tldr: Wright's father Steve advised him to always bring wrestling gear to opportunities, a tip that paid off when Ric Flair needed a last-minute replacement for a WCW event. Wright's impromptu first match impressed management enough to earn him a full-time contract at just 18 years old, launching his tenure with the company.

stories.title: Nikki Cross PROGRESS Promotion Plans
stories.tldr: Nikki Cross and Big Damo are aiming to establish PROGRESS Wrestling as the world's top independent promotion following their recent purchase. Cross wants to showcase European talent and create aggressive, story-driven wrestling while carving out her own path outside WWE.

stories.title: Ryohei Oiwa Wins NJPW G1 Climax 36, Will Challenge IWGP Champion In October
stories.tldr: Ryohei Oiwa defeated Yuya Uemura in a 35-plus minute G1 Climax 36 final to claim his first G1 crown. Oiwa will challenge IWGP Heavyweight Champion Yota Tsuji on October 12 at King of Pro Wrestling rather than waiting for Wrestle Kingdom in January, following a recent trend among G1 winners.

stories.title: Released WWE Star Returns To NJPW, Attacks Former Teammate
stories.tldr: Jeff Cobb returned to NJPW at the G1 Climax 36 tournament final on August 16, his first appearance for the promotion since April 2025. In a shocking moment, Cobb attacked his former United Empire and tag team partner Callum Newman, instead joining the rival Unbound Company faction.

stories.title: Chris Jericho on no longer main eventing AEW
stories.tldr: Chris Jericho has re-signed with AEW and is comfortable moving away from consistent main event spots, crediting the company's roster depth as proof of its growth. Jericho cited his emotional investment in AEW's founding as the key factor in choosing to remain with the promotion rather than return to WWE, while expressing enthusiasm about working with numerous wrestlers still on the roster.

stories.title: Darby Allin's honeymoon thumbtack spot
stories.tldr: Darby Allin took a brutal thumbtack bump just one day after getting married, with the AEW Forbidden Door 2026 multi-man tag match taking place on Sunday while his wedding was Saturday. During the match, MJF flipped Allin face-first into the thumbtacks, and Allin joked that his honeymoon consisted of taking extreme bumps on no sleep. When asked about potential Las Vegas casino stunts, Allin pitched the idea of skateboarding down the Sphere with a bungee cord for safety.

stories.title: Jeff Jarrett's Texas Chain Saw Massacre Death Match Championship reign
stories.tldr: Jeff Jarrett has officially reached three years as AEW's Texas Chain Saw Massacre Death Match Champion, a reign he began by defeating Jeff Hardy on August 16, 2023. The championship run is being heralded as historic and the greatest title reign in AEW history, with Jarrett remaining undefeated in all title defenses during his time as champion.

stories.title: Kyle Fletcher on career goals in AEW
stories.tldr: AEW International Champion Kyle Fletcher has set an ambitious career goal to be remembered as the greatest professional wrestler of all time, even acknowledging the target may be unattainable. The undefeated 2026 star believes this lofty aspiration drives continuous improvement and gives him something to perpetually chase throughout his career, hoping to at least remain in the conversation among wrestling's elite.

stories.title: AEW Grand Slam Mexico gate update
stories.tldr: AEW Grand Slam Mexico generated a live gate of over $600,000 from a sold-out Arena Mexico crowd of approximately 13,000 fans, making it one of the largest television tapings in company history. The event was headlined by Will Ospreay vs. Mark Davis in a Mexico City Street Fight, which received a 4.75-star rating from Dave Meltzer, tying it for the highest-rated match of the show.

stories.title: Jeff Jarrett bucket list venues
stories.tldr: At 59 years old, AEW's Jeff Jarrett revealed that Arena Mexico remains on his professional wrestling bucket list, a venue he has never performed at despite his decades-long career. Jarrett discussed the historic arena's cultural significance in Mexico during an episode of his podcast, noting that CMLL wrestling cannot be replicated elsewhere. While largely retired from full-time competition, Jarrett continues to take his career one day at a time and remains open to occasional appearances.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite August 19 updates and Nigel McGuinness injury
stories.tldr: Nigel McGuinness suffered a legitimate injury during his Continental Challenge Cup victory over Katsuyori Shibata at Collision, forcing AEW to withhold details until Monday's Quarterfinal Selection Special. Will Ospreay will pull double duty on Wednesday's Dynamite, facing the Don Callis Family in two separate six-man tag matches. Kenny Omega and Ospreay will also sit down with Renee Paquette ahead of their All In title showdown.

stories.title: Jim Ross brain surgery update
stories.tldr: Jim Ross shared his first post-surgery photo three days after undergoing brain shunt surgery on August 12, posting an image of his surgical scar with the caption "The proof is in the pudding." He continues to hope he can attend AEW All In in London on August 30, though his contract status with AEW remains uncertain as it's set to expire this month and he has yet to sign a new deal.

stories.title: AEW All In Casino Gauntlet declarations
stories.tldr: Tommaso Ciampa declared for the AEW All In Casino Gauntlet match on AEW Collision, issuing a chilling warning to the first two entrants (Andrade El Idolo and MJF) that they should pray he doesn't draw the No. 3 spot. Komander also declared for the match in a separate segment, adding another threat to the growing field.

stories.title: Will Ospreay and Kenny Omega in action on AEW Dynamite
stories.tldr: Will Ospreay will compete in two trios matches on Wednesday's AEW Dynamite, first with United Empire stablemates Henare and Francesco Akira against the Don Callis Family, then alongside The Young Bucks against another trio. Ospreay and Kenny Omega will also sit down for an interview with Renee Paquette ahead of their AEW World Championship match at All In on August 30.

stories.title: Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods heading to AEW
stories.tldr: Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods have officially signed with AEW, ending months of speculation. The Young Bucks have expressed long-standing interest in feuding with the former New Day members, and there are indications the pair could team with Swerve Strickland for a three-way Trios Championship match at All In: London.

stories.title: Randy Orton vs Cody Rhodes at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event
stories.tldr: Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes will face off at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event on September 6, 2026, at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Georgia. The match was officially announced by SmackDown General Manager Nick Aldis following Orton's attack on Rhodes at SummerSlam, setting up a rematch from their WrestleMania 42 encounter where Orton had previously defeated Rhodes.

stories.title: Bray Wyatt asked father not to call him son in WWE
stories.tldr: Matt Hardy recalled a touching backstage moment where Bray Wyatt asked his father, WWE Hall of Famer Mike Rotunda, not to call him "son" while working together in WWE. Wyatt was concerned about appearing to receive nepotistic favoritism, wanting to ensure he was treated fairly and that his accomplishments weren't attributed to his family connection. The story reflects Wyatt's awareness of how he was perceived backstage and his determination to earn his position on his own merits.

stories.title: WWE trademark filing for new wrestler name
stories.tldr: WWE filed a trademark application for the name "Andi Summers" on August 14 with Lauren A. Dienes-Middlen listed as the company's attorney of record. The filing has no confirmed details about which wrestler the name is intended for. The trademark is part of a broader wave of recent WWE name filings including Alix Brooks, Cruz Montana, and potentially The Mike.

stories.title: Je'Von Evans on becoming friends with Becky Lynch
stories.tldr: Je'Von Evans, 22-year-old WWE Superstar on the main roster since January, has developed an unexpected friendship and mentoring relationship with Becky Lynch after a humorous initial encounter where he joked about her being his "mom." Additionally, Evans recently discovered that he and SmackDown's B-Fab are blood-related cousins through marriage, adding another interesting personal connection within the WWE roster.

stories.title: Chelsea Green discusses favorite match in TNA
stories.tldr: WWE's Chelsea Green revealed that her favorite match of her career was against Allie in TNA, where she lost the Knockouts Championship. Green described that era as pivotal and a time when she was completely carefree as "The Hot Mess" character, allowing her to focus on storytelling rather than just executing moves.

stories.title: CM Punk and Drew McIntyre feud
stories.tldr: Drew McIntyre autographed a rare 1-of-1 WWE trading card by writing "CM Punk smells like cat urine" across the front, creating a unique collectible that blends wrestling rivalry trash talk with official merchandise. The card was pulled by fan Cody James at a card show, turning what would have been a valuable autograph into something far more memorable and potentially more sought-after by collectors who appreciate the personal feud between the two wrestlers.

stories.title: WWE star loses championship in another promotion
stories.tldr: Baron Corbin has lost the MLW World Tag Team Championship in what is being reported as his final match with the promotion following his return to WWE. Corbin, who had previously held the titles as Bishop Dyer alongside Donovan Dijak as the Skyscrapers, dropped the championship to the Good Brothers on an episode of MLW Fusion. The loss comes after Corbin's successful return to WWE, where he captured the United States Championship at SummerSlam.

stories.title: Layla questions WWE's interim label on Chelsea Green's title win
stories.tldr: Former WWE Women's Champion Layla criticized WWE's decision to crown Chelsea Green as Interim Women's Champion rather than simply calling her the champion, arguing that Green deserved to have her moment celebrated without qualifiers. Green won the title at SummerSlam in a five-way ladder match while Rhea Ripley recovered from knee surgery, but subsequently suffered a broken orbital bone days later, complicating the title situation further.

stories.title: Nic Nemeth recalls Brock Lesnar breaking Undertaker's streak
stories.tldr: Nic Nemeth recently recalled the shocking moment when Brock Lesnar defeated The Undertaker's undefeated WrestleMania streak at WrestleMania 30 in 2014, describing the stunned silence that fell over the WWE catering area as the decision was announced. The victory was a pivotal moment that helped solidify Lesnar's legacy and set the stage for his eventual passing of the torch to Oba Femi at SummerSlam 2026.

stories.title: Kevin Owens discusses locker room incident with CM Punk
stories.tldr: Kevin Owens detailed a backstage incident with CM Punk at a Ring of Honor show where tensions arose over Owens' choice to wrestle in a singlet versus a shirt. After being asked by management to wrestle without a shirt, Owens eventually decided to comply, but Punk made a crack about it beforehand. When Owens jokingly asked "Are you happy now?" after his exhausting match, Punk took it as disrespectful and became upset, though Owens clarified they were not actually close to coming to blows despite reports claiming otherwise.

stories.title: Jeff Cobb assesses WWE run as JC Mateo
stories.tldr: Jeff Cobb reflected on his brief WWE run as JC Mateo, which ended with his release on May 2nd, 2026. While acknowledging things could have gone better, Cobb expressed gratitude for the experience, the friendships he made, and his time with the MFTs faction, though he noted discomfort with aspects like being forced to wear face paint, which he never did during his New Japan career.

stories.title: Diana Hart on Vince McMahon creating European Championship
stories.tldr: Diana Hart revealed that Vince McMahon created the European Championship specifically to retain British Bulldog during a period when WCW was actively recruiting established wrestlers. McMahon reportedly told Smith he wanted to "build a belt around" him as an incentive to remain with WWE. While the company's official history confirms Bulldog became the inaugural European Champion in 1997, McMahon's contractual motivations behind the title's creation remain unconfirmed by WWE.

stories.title: JBL on Danhausen
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer JBL praised Danhausen on "Something to Wrestle," acknowledging the young star's remarkable rise to mainstream prominence following his "curse and uncurse" of the New York Knicks, which led to NBA Championship success. Despite calling Danhausen's Elimination Chamber debut in March "the worst thing" in wrestling history, JBL credited his creative abilities and crossover appeal for his current success at major WWE events and in mainstream media.

stories.title: Jacob Fatu on Samoan Werewolf nickname origin
stories.tldr: Jacob Fatu revealed on Stephanie McMahon's podcast that his "Samoan Werewolf" nickname originated from the Twilight franchise character Jacob Black, played by Taylor Lautner. Early in his wrestling career, Fatu was on the same team as trainer Gangrel, who portrayed a vampire character, prompting the werewolf pairing reference. The name stuck and became part of Fatu's wrestling identity.

stories.title: Kevin Nash on Undertaker and WWE Curtain Call
stories.tldr: Kevin Nash defended The Kliq's controversial 1996 Curtain Call incident at Madison Square Garden, claiming Undertaker's criticism stemmed from jealousy rather than legitimate concerns about breaking character. Nash argued the group asked for permission beforehand and that the incident ultimately helped establish the foundation for the Attitude Era. Other wrestlers like Davey Boy Smith were also unhappy about the perceived slight.

stories.title: Tiffany Stratton hopes for Paul Heyman in her corner
stories.tldr: Tiffany Stratton, the current Women's United States Champion, has expressed interest in having Paul Heyman serve as her advocate and manager. Stratton believes Heyman could elevate her career to the next level, similar to what he has done for other talent. Though her original "Daddy's little rich girl" gimmick from NXT was scrapped due to creative unable to find the right male performer, Stratton has thrived on the main roster regardless.

stories.title: Bayley supports AEW's Rebel with ALS Ice Bucket Challenge
stories.tldr: Bayley participated in the ALS Ice Bucket Challenge to support AEW's Rebel, who is battling ALS. After being nominated by Gail Kim and Natalya, Bayley completed the challenge using two buckets and nominated multiple wrestlers and personalities to participate next. The wrestling community continues to rally around Rebel, with a special charity event planned for September 9.

stories.title: AJ Styles identifies WWE NXT performer as future superstar
stories.tldr: AJ Styles recently praised Brooks Jensen, a 24-year-old WWE NXT performer, as a future superstar with exceptional potential. Jensen, the son of former WWE star Bull Buchanan, has impressed Styles with his deep understanding of professional wrestling and dedication to his craft despite recovering from a recent injury. Styles, who now scouts talent for WWE after his retirement from in-ring competition, believes Jensen will become one of the biggest names to emerge from NXT.

stories.title: The Miz names WWE opponents he learned from
stories.tldr: The Miz recently named Randy Orton and John Cena as the two most pivotal figures in his WWE career, crediting them as his greatest learning experiences in the ring. When forced to choose between them, Miz selected Cena, praising his selflessness and the trust he showed by guiding Miz through their WrestleMania main event match. Miz has consistently acknowledged both wrestlers' profound influence on his development as a performer.

stories.title: Jacob Fatu on watching The Usos in jail
stories.tldr: Jacob Fatu revealed that watching The Usos perform on Monday Night RAW while incarcerated became a pivotal moment in his life that motivated him to change his path. Housed on the honor side of a jail facility with about 120 other inmates sharing one television, Fatu witnessed his cousins Jimmy and Jey alongside other family members like Nattie, TJ, and Harry, which made him realize he needed to turn his life around for his wife and children.

stories.title: JBL calls Brock Lesnar greatest of all time
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer JBL recently praised Brock Lesnar as one of the greatest of all time, citing his ability to deliver excellent matches despite working a limited schedule compared to other wrestlers. JBL, who faced Lesnar early in his WWE career, credited the "Beast Incarnate" with having an incredible feel in the ring. While Lesnar has stated he retired at SummerSlam, some WWE officials believe he could return for WrestleMania in Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: Royce Keys recalls WWE Royal Rumble debut
stories.tldr: Royce Keys made his WWE debut as a surprise entrant at the Royal Rumble in Saudi Arabia at the start of the year, recalling the experience as surreal and overwhelming. Despite a grueling 26-hour journey and being confined to his hotel room as a surprise participant, Keys received tremendous support from the locker room and the crowd. Triple H even arranged for weights to be brought to his room so he could continue training before his debut.

stories.title: WWE star addresses tag team split
stories.tldr: Brie Bella has reflected on her tag team partnership with Paige coming to an end following a betrayal by the Bella Twins at SummerSlam, sharing an emotional video and calling it "the end of an era." The split occurred after Paige and Brie held the Women's Tag Team Championship for 91 days before losing to Fatal Influence, with Nikki and Brie attacking Paige after their SummerSlam loss. Brie suffered a broken scapula during the match and is expected to be out for three to six months, while the rivalry between Nikki and Paige continues to intensify on WWE television.

stories.title: Nick Aldis on joining WWE in non-wrestling role
stories.tldr: Nick Aldis joined WWE in 2023 initially in a behind-the-scenes role rather than as an in-ring performer, eventually becoming SmackDown GM. After facing previous rejection and lacking internal advocates like other wrestlers had, Aldis took Diamond Dallas Page's advice to contact Triple H directly, which led to his eventual signing and path to his SummerSlam in-ring debut against GUNTHER.

stories.title: CM Punk wrestles at WWE NXT live event
stories.tldr: CM Punk didn't just appear at the NXT live event in Petersburg, Virginia on August 15 — he wrestled in the main event. Punk teamed with NXT Tag Team Champions Tavion Heights and Myles Borne in a six-man tag match against the Vanity Project, with his team winning after putting Jackson Drake through a table.

stories.title: Blake Monroe's WWE SmackDown debut
stories.tldr: Blake Monroe's match against Giulia has been officially scheduled for next week's SmackDown after Nick Aldis met with her backstage and put an end to her string of unprovoked attacks on the roster. Aldis used the booking as an opportunity to address Monroe's behavior, telling her the backstage beatdowns had to stop. Monroe and Giulia have history from their time in STARDOM, with one of their 2023 matchups considered among Monroe's best performances.

stories.title: R-Truth loses WWE Tag Team Championships
stories.tldr: R-Truth took to social media to apologize to the WWE Universe and his tag team partner Damian Priest following their championship loss. The apology came after their 147-day reign as WWE Tag Team Champions came to an end on SmackDown.

stories.title: Roman Reigns Money in the Bank challenger update
stories.tldr: LA Knight's Money in the Bank title shot against Roman Reigns is gaining momentum with internal WWE confidence the match will happen. Knight's history with Reigns includes two prior title matches, both losses. A recent backstage segment between Knight and Jacob Fatu on Raw suggests The Bloodline storyline may play into the feud.

stories.title: WWE championship win commentary
stories.tldr: Following their WWE Tag Team Championship victory, Tama Tonga declared the MFTs "undeniable" in a post-match video. The win marks Tama's third tag title reign, and comes as the team undergoes roster changes with father Haku now appearing at ringside. Recent departures of JC Mateo and Tonga Loa, plus Solo Sikoa's potential Bloodline reunion, have left Tama and Talla as the faction's core.

stories.title: Cody Rhodes and Oba Femi WWE World Tag Team Championship match
stories.tldr: Cody Rhodes and Oba Femi fell short in their dark match challenge for the WWE World Tag Team Championship after SmackDown, with the match ending in a disqualification when Maxxine Dupri attacked Rhodes. Despite the loss, the two babyfaces stood tall after disposing of their opponents. Meanwhile, Rhodes is now embroiled in a separate feud with Randy Orton on the singles side.

stories.title: Matt Hardy on not rushing Zilla Fatu into The Bloodline
stories.tldr: Matt Hardy believes Zilla Fatu should spend an extended period—potentially a full year—in NXT to develop his individual character before joining The Bloodline on the main roster. Hardy emphasized that Fatu needs time to learn WWE's television system and establish his own identity separate from the broader Samoan faction.

stories.title: Shinsuke Nakamura tag team partner revealed
stories.tldr: Shinsuke Nakamura's mystery tag team partner has been revealed as Hiromu Takahashi, the former NJPW star known as "The Ticking Time Bomb." Nakamura's latest promo used that exact phrase to describe his partner, strongly indicating the recently WWE-signed Japanese wrestler will challenge the Tongas for the tag titles.

stories.title: Penta and Perros del Mal storyline on AAA on Fox
stories.tldr: During the August 15 episode of AAA on Fox, Perros del Mal approached Penta with an offer to rejoin their faction ahead of his tournament run for a shot at Roman Reigns' WWE World Heavyweight Championship. After Penta questioned whether newer members Bronco Nima and Karmen Petrovic had earned their place, Nima challenged him to a match on August 22 with the stipulation that Penta must rejoin the group if he loses.

stories.title: Josh Bishop drawing TNA interest after WWE tryout
stories.tldr: Josh Bishop has drawn interest from TNA Wrestling following his recent WWE tryout during SummerSlam week in August. The independent wrestler currently works with MLW as part of the Skyscrapers tag team with Donovan Dijak and has previous experience with 4th Rope Wrestling. Bishop's situation is notable because he could potentially have MLW matches still airing on television while simultaneously appearing for TNA shortly after his WWE tryout, putting him in an unusual position with multiple major companies paying attention to his career.

stories.title: AAA Heroes Inmortales 2026 announcement
stories.tldr: Lucha Libre AAA announced Heroes Inmortales 2026 will take place on October 24, 2026, at the Gimnasio Olímpico Juan de la Barrera in Mexico City. This will be the 18th edition of the annual event held in tribute to late AAA founder Antonio Pena. The announcement came minutes after the August 15, 2026 episode of AAA on Fox, with tickets already available for purchase.

stories.title: La Parka advances in Roman Reigns World title tournament
stories.tldr: La Parka advanced to the second round of a tournament to determine Roman Reigns' challenger for the WWE World Heavyweight Championship on September 14, 2026, in Mexico City. During his first-round match against Psycho Clown on the August 15 episode of AAA on Fox, a mysterious masked man attacked Clown while the referee was incapacitated, allowing La Parka to finish his opponent and advance. La Parka will face Penta in the second round.

stories.title: Joe Gacy wins GCW World Championship
stories.tldr: Joseph Sawyer, formerly known as Joe Gacy from his WWE tenure, won the GCW World Championship at GCW Homecoming Night One by defeating Atticus Cogar in a chaotic main event. The match featured interference from Drake Wuertz and the revelation of Max Recon as a VNDL associate, with Sawyer finishing Cogar with Sister Abigail. This marks Sawyer's first GCW World Championship reign, ending Cogar's impressive 267-day title run that included 25 successful title defenses.

stories.title: Alex Wright on WCW Power Plant experience
stories.tldr: During a recent interview, Alex Wright discussed his formative years at the WCW Power Plant, revealing that trainers may have intentionally pushed him to test his mental resolve. Wright also reflected on WCW's decline, noting that wrestlers could see the company deteriorating through poor booking decisions made by people without in-ring experience, and observable signs like artificially rearranging fans to make venues appear full.

stories.title: Aaron Wolf pulled from NJPW G1 Climax 36
stories.tldr: Aaron Wolf has been pulled from the NJPW G1 Climax 36 final show on August 16th due to a health-related issue. The NEVER Openweight Champion competed the previous night on August 15th in a losing effort alongside Tatsuya Matsumoto and Oleg Boltin against T.M.D.K. Wolf finished the tournament with eight points in the B block, and Yuya Uemura will now face Ryohei Oiwa in the final to determine the G1 Climax 36 winner.

stories.title: Kay Lee Ray returning to ICW Scotland
stories.tldr: Kay Lee Ray is returning to Insane Championship Wrestling for the promotion's 20th Anniversary Event on October 20th. The former three-time ICW Women's World Champion, who was a staple of the promotion from 2012 to 2019, has rejoined the independent scene following the end of her WWE tenure. ICW announced her homecoming with considerable fanfare, billing her as an iconic figure in the promotion's history.

stories.title: JBL backs AJ Styles' son in GCW chair incident
stories.tldr: JBL defended Avery Styles after controversy erupted when the 19-year-old AJ Styles' son declined to help set up chairs at a GCW event in Minneapolis. JBL argued that if setup duties weren't communicated as part of the booking, Avery was right to refuse, citing his own experience paying dues in the territories. Rather than let the dispute fade, JBL suggested WWE capitalize on the controversy by turning it into a storyline with Avery as a babyface and Arik Cannon as the heel.

stories.title: Eric Bischoff on nWo's legacy
stories.tldr: Eric Bischoff reflected on the nWo's 30th anniversary, stating that no faction will ever replicate what the group achieved due to unique historical circumstances of the Monday Night Wars era. Bischoff expressed contentment with his life outside wrestling and explained how the nWo meant different things to its members, with Hulk Hogan's heel turn being particularly significant given his decades-long commitment to his babyface persona.

stories.title: Matt Hardy on Dominik Mysterio's accomplishments
stories.tldr: Matt Hardy praised Dominik Mysterio for accomplishing what many second-generation wrestlers struggle with: creating his own distinct identity separate from his famous father Rey Mysterio. Hardy credited Dominik's heel turn and character development, particularly through storylines with Rhea Ripley and Liv Morgan, for establishing him as a compelling character with genuine heat and emotional investment from fans. Hardy contrasted Dominik's success with other second-generation wrestlers like David Flair and Eric Watts, emphasizing the importance of finding an original identity rather than trying to replicate a legendary predecessor.

stories.title: Hiroshi Tenzan retirement
stories.tldr: Legendary Japanese wrestler Hiroshi Tenzan retired after 35 years in the business, marking the end of an era for one of the biggest stars of the mid-90s and 2000s. The show also covered G-1 Climax semifinals action, Chelsea Green's strong microphone work against Gunther on WWE Smackdown, and analysis of WWE's current booking issues regarding lack of stakes rather than general creative direction.

stories.title: Elijah on working for Vince McMahon in WWE
stories.tldr: Elijah, formerly known as Elias in WWE, reflected on his time working under Vince McMahon, crediting the former chairman for teaching him that wrestlers must take creative challenges and elevate them into memorable performances. He cited John Cena as a prime example of someone who would receive basic creative direction and transform it into something special, a mindset he has carried throughout his career.

stories.title: AI Antonio Inoki at NJPW G1 Climax 36
stories.tldr: An AI recreation of late NJPW founder Antonio Inoki made a surprise appearance on the video screen at G1 Climax 36 semifinals, delivering motivational remarks to wrestlers and fans while promoting upcoming Wrestle Kingdom events. The AI Inoki project, developed by multiple companies including the Inoki Genki Factory, aims to preserve and pass on Inoki's legacy and thinking to future generations for the next 100 years.

stories.title: Big Damo expected to remain with MLW
stories.tldr: Big Damo, the former WWE NXT wrestler known as Killian Dain, has agreed to a contract extension with Major League Wrestling and is expected to remain with the promotion. The 41-year-old made his MLW debut in April 2026 and recently competed in the Opera Cup tournament. Damo and his wife Nikki Storm, the former Nikki Cross, are also co-owners of PROGRESS Wrestling and DEFY Wrestling.

stories.title: Is It Over For Giulia In WWE?
stories.tldr: Giulia arrived in WWE with massive expectations after years of pursuit, winning the NXT Women's Championship in early 2025, but her main roster push has stalled significantly with poor booking and diminishing importance, raising questions about whether her WWE experiment can still succeed.

stories.title: Dean Malenko’s Daughter Marie Gets Another WWE Name Change Ahead of Developmental Run
stories.tldr: Dean Malenko's daughter Marie has been given another ring name change by WWE just months after her initial introduction. Originally announced as Lacey Simon when she joined the Performance Center in May, she will now go by Kenzie. The rebranding comes as Marie prepares for her developmental run after previously competing in Japan.

stories.title: 2 Cold Scorpio Returning to the Ring Weeks After Pleading Guilty in Assault Case
stories.tldr: 2 Cold Scorpio is returning to professional wrestling on August 29 with a match against MASADA in Los Angeles, just weeks after pleading guilty to second-degree assault and armed criminal action. The 60-year-old wrestling veteran, who last competed in August 2025, will make his SVN Wrestling debut while awaiting sentencing scheduled for October 9. His comeback comes more than two years after a June 2024 confrontation incident at a Kansas City travel stop where he was working security.

stories.title: Tiffany Stratton Caught in SWAT Prank During Livestream With N3on
stories.tldr: WWE star Tiffany Stratton was training with Kick streamer N3on at an Arsenal Boxing gym when Los Angeles police suddenly arrived in response to a fake SWAT call targeting N3on's livestream. N3on revealed he receives these prank calls roughly 50 times while streaming in the city, as callers use voice changers to report fake emergencies at his location. The situation was resolved without arrests, and the livestream eventually resumed after police asked the cameras to be turned off.

stories.title: Lio Rush Pulled From PW Revolver Show After Flight Nightmare
stories.tldr: Lio Rush was forced to miss his scheduled PW Revolver appearance after experiencing a travel day plagued by multiple flight delays that culminated in a cancellation. Rush announced the news on social media Saturday night, expressing frustration about missing the event but apologizing to fans and promising to make it up to them. The incident highlights the challenges independent wrestlers face when juggling multiple bookings across different promotions with tight schedules.

stories.title: WWE Hall of Famer JBL says he “beyond hated” Steve Austin’s “What” promos
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer JBL recently discussed Steve Austin's iconic "What" catchphrase on a podcast, revealing he "beyond hated" the promo during its peak in 2001. JBL credited Bill DeMott with creating the catchphrase and acknowledged that while it was frustrating for other performers, he took pride in his ability to overcome audience hijacking attempts during his own promos.

stories.title: Joe Gacy Credits Shawn Michaels For WWE NXT Character, Says Vince McMahon Intervened
stories.tldr: Joe Gacy revealed that Shawn Michaels created his initial politically correct character on NXT, which was designed to eventually evolve into an unsettling cult leader persona. Despite initial backstage approval, Vince McMahon became upset over negative headlines and temporarily pulled Gacy from TV, but later changed his mind after watching the promo himself. Gacy's character eventually evolved through the Schism faction and ultimately led to his involvement with the Wyatt Sicks.

stories.title: Rookie Spotlight: Colt Johnson
stories.tldr: Colt Johnson is an Ohio native who broke into professional wrestling just two years ago after graduating high school, starting his career at his own graduation party where MEGA wrestling trained and featured him. Despite his youth and limited experience, the 20-year-old has already impressed veteran observers with natural talent and athleticism that far exceeds his tenure in the industry, and has even secured a sponsorship deal with Bucked Up supplements.

stories.title: NJPW G1 Climax 36 tournament final
stories.tldr: Yuya Uemura defeated IWGP Heavyweight Champion Yota Tsuji in the first semifinal, while Ryohei Oiwa defeated Callum Newman in the second. The two runners-up from their respective blocks will meet Sunday for the G1 trophy and a guaranteed IWGP Championship shot, with both seeking their first G1 victory.

stories.title: Dominik Mysterio vs El Grande Americano at AAA Triplemania 34
stories.tldr: AAA officially confirmed that Dominik Mysterio will defend the AAA Mega Championship against El Grande Americano on Night 2 of Triplemania 34, taking place September 13 in Mexico City. The match was announced on the August 15 episode of AAA on Fox, with a backstage brawl between the two competitors breaking out that required Rey Mysterio to separate them.

stories.title: WWE News: Blake Monroe’s Debut Opponent Set, WWE Main Roster Talent Crossovers To Continue, More
stories.tldr: Following SmackDown on August 14, WWE released multiple digital exclusives advancing several storylines, including Ricky Starks pursuing Rey Fenix for the AAA Cruiserweight Championship, another teaser for a Shinsuke Nakamura mystery opponent, and backstage interaction with Matt Cardona after his match with Gunther.

stories.title: Nixon Newell AEW Collision Walkout Controversy
stories.tldr: Nixon Newell (formerly Tegan Nox) broke her silence on the November 2025 AEW Collision walkout with Miranda Alize, clarifying that reports about the incident were based on assumptions rather than facts. She revealed the disagreement was about match time—they were promised at least six minutes but received only three—not about refusing to lose. Newell disclosed that she received daily death threats for approximately four months following the controversy, which she says accelerated her decision to retire in 2026.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite Watch Party London
stories.tldr: AEW announced a free public watch party for AEW Dynamite on August 26 at Fulham Pier in London, where fans can watch that night's episode from Glasgow on a big screen. The event runs from 5-10 PM BST and will be hosted by Paul Wight and Jeff Jarrett, who will take photos with fans from 5:30-6:30 PM. Registration is required to attend, and the watch party is part of AEW All In: London week, which culminates with the All In pay-per-view at Wembley Stadium on August 30.

stories.title: Mick Foley and Darby Allin AEW
stories.tldr: Mick Foley has discussed how Darby Allin drew inspiration from his Cactus Jack character and evolved it with superior athleticism to create his own hybrid style. Both have expressed openness to wrestling each other in AEW, with Allin comparing the possibility to Sting's unexpected return from retirement and calling a match between them "insane" in the best way possible.

stories.title: Eddie Kingston AEW Indie Event Pullout
stories.tldr: Eddie Kingston has been pulled from C4 Wrestling's Fighting Back 2026 charity event scheduled for Friday, August 14 in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. The indie promotion cited "circumstances beyond our control" for the last-minute cancellation. Kingston was set to compete in a six-man tag team match alongside Ortiz and Gabriel Fuerza, and the show benefits the Canadian Cancer Society.

stories.title: AEW Grand Slam Mexico and Dynamite Coverage
stories.tldr: Chris Jericho appeared on Wrestling Observer Radio to discuss AEW Grand Slam Mexico, his current run with AEW, and his role as executive producer on a wrestling documentary called VietSlam. The episode also covered historical wrestling topics including an unmade 1965 dream match between Bruno Sammartino and Lou Thesz, and discussions about potential matches between the Funk brothers and G1 semifinals.

stories.title: WWE Expected Offer for AEW-CMLL Champion
stories.tldr: WWE is expected to make an offer to Persephone, the CMLL World Women's Champion who currently holds a dual contract with CMLL and AEW, once her contract expires. Dave Meltzer reports that WWE officials hold Persephone in high regard and would "absolutely" pursue her, though she may face retention efforts from both CMLL and AEW. Persephone has been a regular fixture on AEW programming while maintaining her championship status in CMLL.

stories.title: Yung Money AEW Collision Appearance
stories.tldr: Rising independent tag team Yung Money recently appeared on AEW Collision and will main event Phoenix Championship Wrestling's Anniversary 8 on September 19, 2026, facing the Pretty City Express for the PCW Tag Team Championships in a 2 out of 3 falls match. The team, consisting of Jaden Monroe and RJ Wylde, believe this is a crucial opportunity to finally capture the titles after months of chasing their rivals, with the event expected to be the largest independent wrestling show in Arizona history.

stories.title: ROH Title Contender Nick Wayne AEW Dynamite
stories.tldr: Nick Wayne, the ROH World Title No. 1 contender set to challenge Bandido for the championship next Friday at Death Before Dishonor, took a loss on AEW Dynamite in a three-way match. Dave Meltzer explained that the decision to have Wayne take the pin was made because Mike Bailey has a higher ranking in AEW, though Wayne should theoretically be ranked higher given his title shot status. This reflects Tony Khan's pattern of not protecting ROH champions outside of ROH programming.

stories.title: AEW Hiring Behind-Scenes Roles
stories.tldr: AEW is expanding its behind-the-scenes operations by hiring for two new positions: a Producer, Motion Graphics role in Nashville focused on television post-production, and an Accounting Manager for Live Events position in Jacksonville handling financial responsibilities for touring operations. Both openings reflect the company's commitment to maintaining quality production standards and efficient event management as it continues its full television and touring schedule.

stories.title: AEW All In London 2026 Men's Casino Gauntlet
stories.tldr: AEW All In London 2026 takes place on August 30 at Wembley Stadium, featuring the Men's Casino Gauntlet match with a guaranteed AEW World Title shot for the winner. The article highlights seven potential winners including MJF, Tommaso Ciampa, Komander, "Jungle" Jack Perry, Chris Jericho, Speedball Mike Bailey, and Andrade El Idolo, who is positioned as the top contender.

stories.title: MJF Roman Reigns Nickname Distance
stories.tldr: MJF has aggressively pushed back against fans using the acronym "OTC" for his new "One True Champion" gimmick, demanding people never acronym the monicker and dismissing merchandise comparisons to Roman Reigns' "Original Tribal Chief" nickname. Meanwhile, reports confirm MJF was always planned for AEW All In's Casino Gauntlet match rather than challenging for the World Championship, with both he and Andrade El Idolo set to be focal points of that bout.

stories.title: AEW Jeff Jarrett on WWE Star Direction
stories.tldr: Jeff Jarrett has publicly advised Dominik Mysterio to advocate for himself creatively within WWE, suggesting he's established enough in his career to demand a different direction. Jarrett noted the stark contrast between Mysterio's prominent booking as AAA Mega Champion versus his diminished role on WWE television, where he's posted a 3-20 record this year.

stories.title: Former WWE Stars to Join AEW
stories.tldr: Kingston and Woods are now expected to debut at AEW's All In London event at Wembley Stadium on August 30, where they could face Adam Copeland and Christian Cage in a potential tag team match. AEW is also targeting other recently departed WWE talents including Sheamus, Bayley, and Kairi Sane to strengthen its roster ahead of the show.

stories.title: AEW All In MJF and Andrade Plans
stories.tldr: Wrestling insiders are discussing the potential AEW debut of former New Day members at the All In event. The podcast covered this topic alongside other major wrestling news including creative concerns with The Bloodline storyline and analysis of recent Dark Side of the Ring episodes.

stories.title: Jacob Fatu WWE Second Chance and Addiction
stories.tldr: Jacob Fatu has opened up about nearly losing his WWE opportunity before he was even hired due to personal addiction issues. Triple H ultimately gave him a second chance, and after competing at WrestleMania 42 (a number with special cultural significance to Fatu), the two shared an emotional backstage encounter where Triple H credited Fatu with doing the work himself. The story highlights themes of redemption, personal responsibility, and the importance of second chances.

stories.title: Jacy Jayne Wins Women's United States Championship
stories.tldr: Jacy Jayne won the WWE Women's United States Championship on the August 14, 2026 episode of SmackDown, defeating defending champion Tiffany Stratton with help from her Fatal Influence stablemates. The finish saw Stratton choose to protect interim WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green at ringside rather than secure victory, allowing Jayne to capitalize with a Rolling Encore for the pinfall. This marks a major championship moment for the 30-year-old, who is one of the most decorated wrestlers in NXT history.

stories.title: MFTs Win WWE Tag Team Championship
stories.tldr: Tama Tonga and Talla Tonga won the WWE Tag Team Championship on August 14 SmackDown in a triple threat match, defeating defending champions Damian Priest and R-Truth along with The War Raiders. The victory marked Talla's first WWE title while Tama earned his third tag team championship. The MFTs' father Haku, who recently returned to WWE, was at ringside to celebrate the win.

stories.title: Pat McAfee Music Album Release
stories.tldr: Pat McAfee, the former WWE commentator, has officially released his debut album "The Diary Of A Polarizing Figure" on August 14, 2026, after spending two decades writing songs about his life and experiences. The 14-track, 42-minute project is available on Spotify and YouTube and follows his 2025 single "Dookie." While some sports personalities praised the album, it has drawn significant criticism from fans and social media users questioning McAfee's decision to pursue music.

stories.title: Shinsuke Nakamura Tag Team Partner Tease
stories.tldr: Shinsuke Nakamura has teased a mystery tag team partner to challenge the newly crowned MFTs (Tama Tonga and Talla Tonga) for the WWE Tag Team Championship. In a post-SmackDown digital exclusive, Nakamura described his partner as a "ticking time bomb" who is experienced, vicious, and deadly—language that strongly suggests the partner is Hiromu Takahashi, the former IWPW Junior Heavyweight Champion who departed New Japan Pro Wrestling in February and is expected to have signed with WWE.

stories.title: Paige SmackDown Segment Cut
stories.tldr: Paige's scheduled WWE SmackDown promo was cut from the August 14 broadcast, prompting her to react on social media with criticism about women's segments being eliminated. She fired back at Nikki Bella's claims about revitalizing her career, and WWE later posted the unaired promo as a digital exclusive while the feud between the two wrestlers continues online and heading into the following week's show.

stories.title: August 14 WWE SmackDown Title Changes and Results
stories.tldr: The August 14, 2026 episode of WWE SmackDown in Boston featured two title changes as the MFTs won the WWE World Tag Team Championship in a three-way match, and Jacy Jayne of Fatal Influence captured the WWE Women's United States Championship from Tiffany Stratton. The show also saw Baron Corbin retain his United States Championship against Carmelo Hayes, while General Manager Nick Aldis gave Chelsea Green 30 days to get medically cleared or risk losing her WWE Women's Interim Championship.

stories.title: The Rock Under Armour Partnership End
stories.tldr: Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson has ended his 10-year partnership with Under Armour, which produced the Project Rock clothing and footwear line featuring his signature Brahma Bull logo. The split was amicable, with Under Armour continuing to distribute existing inventory through October 2026. Johnson and his ex-wife and business partner Dany Garcia, who own the Project Rock trademark, are now seeking a new manufacturing partner to continue the brand.

stories.title: Jerry Lawler Bill Dundee One More Match
stories.tldr: Jerry Lawler has teased the possibility of one more match with Bill Dundee during a Memphis Wrestling event in Tupelo, Mississippi benefiting St. Jude Children's Research Hospital. While no match has been officially announced, Lawler has previously stated he hasn't ruled out returning to the ring despite suffering two strokes in recent years and rating his health at around six or seven out of ten.

stories.title: Baron Corbin Retains Men's US Title
stories.tldr: Baron Corbin successfully retained the WWE United States Championship against Carmelo Hayes on SmackDown, hitting End of Days for the victory. However, the celebration was short-lived as Trick Williams emerged and Lil Yachty attacked Corbin with a kendo stick, with Williams following up with a Trick Shot to stand tall over the champion, setting up further tensions between the rivals.

stories.title: Johnny Knoxville and Sami Zayn Feud
stories.tldr: Johnny Knoxville posted a fake apology video to Sami Zayn while promoting his latest Jackass film, only to immediately continue insulting him. Zayn fired back with a brutal response, wishing Knoxville would suffer another traumatic brain injury while watching the movie, escalating their long-running feud that began after their WrestleMania 39 match.

stories.title: Trick Williams CM Punk Comparison
stories.tldr: Trick Williams has declared himself a superior trash-talker to CM Punk, claiming his natural ability to talk trash has been passed down through his DNA and extends back decades beyond either competitor's lifetime. Following his loss of the United States Championship to Baron Corbin at SummerSlam, Williams expressed interest in pursuing Money in the Bank and reclaiming his title, while remaining open to a verbal confrontation with Punk.

stories.title: Trick Williams and The Undertaker NXT Confrontation
stories.tldr: Trick Williams revealed that his aggressive promo confrontation with The Undertaker on NXT was completely improvised, with no backstage discussion beforehand about what he would say or how Undertaker would respond. Williams called it his "most risky work," throwing out a bold threat without knowing if it would backfire, but the gamble paid off as he earned Undertaker's respect before taking a chokeslam. The segment was particularly meaningful for Williams, who had been terrified of Undertaker as a child and never even selected him in wrestling video games.

stories.title: Cody Rhodes Future Plans
stories.tldr: Cody Rhodes plans to continue his wrestling career until Brodie Lee Jr., the teenage son of late AEW star Brodie Lee, is ready to have a match with him, potentially taking breaks and returning as needed. In separate comments, Rhodes also revealed that his iconic neck tattoo, the American Nightmare logo, is his greatest regret in life due to its unexpected size and placement, though it has become inseparable from his brand and merchandise.

stories.title: Randy Orton Interrupts Cody Rhodes vs Sami Zayn
stories.tldr: Randy Orton attacked Cody Rhodes before the scheduled main event against Sami Zayn could begin on the August 14 episode of WWE SmackDown, turning the match into a brawl that spilled outside the ring. The altercation continued through the crowd and back toward ringside, ultimately forcing officials to intervene and causing the main event to be scrapped entirely, leaving Sami Zayn unable to compete as planned.

stories.title: Shawn Michaels Photo Revisit
stories.tldr: Shawn Michaels recently participated in a WWE challenge where young talents recreated iconic wrestler poses. When Michaels drew himself, he humorously recreated his famous 1996 Playgirl pictorial pose with the WWF Championship, later joking on Instagram that he should have known better than to trust the options provided.

stories.title: Jeff Cobb WWE Offers
stories.tldr: Jeff Cobb turned down WWE's contract offers on three separate occasions before finally accepting on the fourth attempt. His reasons ranged from not wanting to relocate to Florida, to having recently signed with New Japan, to finding a FaceTime call with an executive amusing.
